title: Neuropsychologists
description: Apply theories and principles of neuropsychology to evaluate and diagnose disorders of higher cerebral functioning, often in research and medical settings. Study the human brain and the effect of physiological states on human cognition and behavior. May formulate and administer programs of treatment.

tasks.text: Conduct neuropsychological evaluations such as assessments of intelligence, academic ability, attention, concentration, sensorimotor function, language, learning, and memory.
tasks.rationale: interpersonal — Proctoring and standardized administration need human presence

dwas.name: Administer standardized physical or psychological tests.

tasks.text: Write or prepare detailed clinical neuropsychological reports, using data from psychological or neuropsychological tests, self-report measures, rating scales, direct observations, or interviews.
tasks.rationale: text generation — Reports drafted; presentations need human delivery

dwas.name: Prepare scientific or technical reports or presentations.

tasks.text: Interview patients to obtain comprehensive medical histories.
tasks.rationale: interpersonal — Observation and interviews are inherently human

dwas.name: Collect information from people through observation, interviews, or surveys.

tasks.text: Diagnose and treat conditions involving injury to the central nervous system, such as cerebrovascular accidents, neoplasms, infectious or inflammatory diseases, degenerative diseases, head traumas, demyelinating diseases, and various forms of dementing illnesses.
tasks.rationale: decision support — Neuro/psych diagnosis needs interview, testing, clinical accountability

tasks.text: Establish neurobehavioral baseline measures for monitoring progressive cerebral disease or recovery.
tasks.rationale: decision support — AI drafts care standards; clinical authority decides

dwas.name: Establish standards for medical care.
